summary: SL-053 removed the two hard-coded settled counts from tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 (C-001 line 205, C-003 line 268). Both cases were already red on entry (28 expected vs 32 seen; 29 vs 33). A lazy, memoised Get-ExpectedSettled now counts the `rules:` items in .taad/fitness.yaml and subtracts a single $Twinned = 15. A guard rule in fitness.yaml forbids re-pinning. The build deviated from the design in two ways. A person's O-015 decision replaced the design's oracle (Fitness rule count shared with C-007) with a direct yaml count. The 'throwaway' probe became a permanent 9-shape script, SettledCountProbe.ps1 (96 s), because the owed cases had to be discharged by a persistent test. Validation found nothing wrong. Nothing in the engine reruns either the suite or the probe.

learned.lesson: The settled count is the number of `  - name:` items under `rules:` in .taad/fitness.yaml minus the 15 twinned entries. It is NOT the number of `# settled by SL-nnn` markers: markers are per slice, and one slice can append several entries under one marker. Any future check on these counts must count items.
learned.evidence: 3 markers covered 4 new entries between 28 and 32. The AppendTwo probe shape (two entries under one marker) stays green. Independent count of `^  - name:` gave 48 = Fitness's 48 rules = 15 twinned + 33 settled.

learned.lesson: Facts (11), twinned (15) and patterns (27) are still literal in many places. A slice that adds a twinned entry (a new Fact) must hand-edit $Twinned/11/27 in RuleCases C-001, C-003, C-004 and C-005, C-008's 14/15 pins, and SettledCountProbe.ps1 (Get-Line at :124-126, default $twinned = 15). Nothing gate-visible fails if one is missed. The new guard rule only covers the settled-count pattern in RuleCases.ps1.
learned.evidence: Build and code-review 'left open' lists. The probe pins 11/15/27 a second time and the exact source text of eng/rules-parity.ps1:632-633.

learned.lesson: The engine appends a slice's declared architecture_rules to .taad/fitness.yaml at design acceptance, so the tree at build time is already larger than the survey's (32 measured, 33 at build). Counts written in a design are stale on arrival. A rule's `because` text is also frozen at design time and the builder should not hand-edit it, so it drifts when a later decision changes the mechanism. Write `because` text that names the constraint, not the derivation.
learned.evidence: The guard rule's because still says 'Fitness rule count minus the twinned count' after O-015 switched to a direct yaml count. The code-review filed it as drift (fitness.yaml:600-604). It is numerically true (48 = 48), so it was left.

learned.lesson: Every `case` in a design becomes an obligation that only a persistent test command the engine runs can discharge. A design that plans a 'throwaway, not committed' probe for its cases will be turned into a permanent script at build. Size a test-bookkeeping slice's cases to what should live in the repo. Here 11 owed cases for a two-literal fix produced a 96 s, 9-shape script that also adds new pin surface.
learned.evidence: Design: 'Growth-and-bite probe (throwaway, not committed)'. Build deviation: 'The probe is permanent... obligations O-002 to O-011 must be discharged by a test command the engine runs'. SettledCountProbe.ps1 was added.

learned.lesson: When a design's central premise is a must-verify that costs one command (here: run `-Case C-007`, run C-001 as a lone `-Case`), run it in design or build-check instead of owing it. The C-007-derived oracle was designed, marked as a decidable disagreement, then overruled by a person (O-015) and never built. The 'Fitness rule-count source (shared with C-007)' component was designed and deliberately not built. C-007 needs -EnginePython/-EngineRoot and about 52 s, while C-001 runs in 3 s with no engine arguments. The text of O-015 is clipped in this record, so that is the likely reason, not a confirmed one.
learned.evidence: O-010, O-012, O-013 and O-015 in the obligations list. Build 'left open': 'Case-C007 was not modified... the design's component is therefore deliberately not built'.

learned.lesson: Obligation ids collide between scopes. Design, build and validate all cite 'O-005 (from the SL-031 reflection)' as open (no gate runs RuleCases). SL-053's own O-005 (C-001 fails on a non-AGREE verdict) is discharged. Refer to the project-level gap by name ('rules suite is not run by any gate'), not by O-nnn.
learned.evidence: The obligations list shows O-005 as [case] discharged. The build, code-review and validate 'left open' entries all call O-005 open.

learned.lesson: Reflection-born slices arrive as one sentence with no acceptance list, and the build-check writes its own criteria. Because nothing is built yet, every criterion is 'missing', so the first build-check halts and needs a person to say 'build anyway'. Expect that halt on the next slice of this kind. Do not put counts in candidate text: '7 settled' was 21 entries stale when the slice opened (28 in the file, 32 in the tree).
learned.evidence: build-check #1 halted, #2 'built anyway despite a partial survey'. Rework line: build-check ran 2 times. The slice note says '7 settled'; the file said 28.

learned.lesson: Run costs to size any 'wire the suite into a gate' work: C-001 about 3 s, C-003 about 6 s, C-007 about 52 s (needs the engine venv and root), SettledCountProbe -Shape All 96 s, full RuleCases -Case All 233 s (it builds the solution through eng/dotnet.ps1). Only the engine-free cases are plausible for a per-slice gate.
learned.evidence: Timings in the build and validate records for those commands.

learned.lesson: Because no gate runs tests/rules, C-001 and C-003 went red unseen across SL-044, SL-046 and SL-047 (28 to 32 settled) after SL-043 hand-refreshed them. This slice fixed the settled pin but not the invisibility. 'Stays green after the next real engine append' was only simulated on scratch copies. The next slice that declares architecture_rules is the first live test: run C-001 and C-003 there, expecting settled = rules items minus 15.
learned.evidence: Build-check: C-001 exit 1 with 4 failures, C-003 with 2, on the untouched tree. Validate 'not reached': 'simulated on scratch copies, not observed'.

learned.lesson: RuleCases cases are run under both powershell.exe 5.1 and pwsh 7, and the oracle needed explicit handling for both. Take exit codes from $LASTEXITCODE directly after the call, never through a pipe. The build-check's C-003 run piped into Select-String and lost its exit code (null).
learned.evidence: Build-check command list: the C-003 entry has exit_code null. The BothShells probe shape runs a yaml cut to exactly one settled entry to exercise 5.1's scalar unrolling.

candidates.title: Run the engine-free RuleCases (C-001 to C-005) from an engine gate, and decide whether SettledCountProbe rides along, so pin drift fails in the slice that causes it
candidates.why: This slice exists because C-001 and C-003 sat red across SL-044, SL-046 and SL-047 with no gate running the suite. The design, build and validate all left this open. The slice added a 96 s probe and 9-shape coverage that nothing reruns after commit. It is now the only unguarded seam in the settled-count fix. C-001 takes about 3 s and C-003 about 6 s, so a per-slice run is cheap for the engine-free cases and expensive for the 233 s full suite.

candidates.title: One source for the parity-summary pins (11 facts, 15 twinned, 27 patterns) across RuleCases and SettledCountProbe. Make the probe's mutations stop depending on the exact source text of eng/rules-parity.ps1:632-633
candidates.why: Code-review recorded that the probe pins the three literals a second time and pins the tool's source lines. A slice that adds a twinned entry currently hand-edits about six places, and an innocent edit to line 633 of rules-parity.ps1 breaks five probe shapes. The trigger is the next slice that adds a twinned entry.

candidates.title: Remove machine-specific engine paths (%APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe, C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend) from the C-007 test command and the full-suite command
candidates.why: Build and validate both list this. C-007 and the full suite were only run on this machine at engine revision 020811e. Another machine or engine revision was never tried, and this blocks any gate wiring that does not run here.

payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium size, low risk, one designer. The low risk tier was right about the product: nothing in PS-001..PS-007 or R-001..R-007 was touched, the build was one attempt with no loop, and validation's own four mutations found no defect. It was wrong about what the tier implied. Critique and critique-review were skipped as no-ops (both recorded no account), yet the design carried a person-decision fork (O-015) that overturned its central oracle, and a contract gap with the engine's obligation model (a throwaway probe against durable-test obligations). The fix itself is about 25 lines of oracle plus two edited lines, so medium held only because the 11 owed cases, the probe and the guard rule are verification overhead. Size the next test-bookkeeping slice by its owed cases, not by its diff. The tier was also wrong the other way for the survey: the build-check halted once on a not-yet-built slice, which cost a human override.

missed.what: The design promised to cover 9 of its owed cases with a 'throwaway, not committed' build-time probe. It did not ask how a [case] obligation is discharged: only by a persistent test command the engine runs. The build had to make the probe permanent (SettledCountProbe.ps1, 9 shapes, 96 s). It carries a second copy of 11/15/27 and pins rules-parity.ps1:632-633 source text, which is new pin surface in a slice meant to remove pins. The critique was a no-op at low tier, so this measures the tier decision, not a review that looked and missed. A check to write: for any design whose cases rely on a probe 'not committed', ask which command the engine will run to discharge each owed case.
missed.caught_by: build (declared as deviation 'The probe is permanent, not a throwaway'), then code-review recorded the extra pins as drift

unknowns: Does C-001/C-003 stay green on the first REAL engine append after SL-053? Growth was only simulated on scratch copies. The oracle counts items at the first item's indent, so it depends on the engine's append format (indent, marker comment) not changing.
Does SettledCountProbe run correctly with powershell.exe 5.1 as the OUTER shell? Validate drove it only from pwsh, and only its GuardRule shape was checked under 5.1.

Does the probe's GuardRule shape survive commit-slice's merge or rebase and a fresh or shallow clone? It reads the pre-fix RuleCases.ps1 from a fixed commit, 0647ead17. If that commit is not reachable, the shape fails and needs a new anchor.
Which RuleCases cases can run in a gate without the engine venv/root paths or an eng/dotnet.ps1 solution build? This has to be known before the gate-wiring work is designed.
What happens on a slice that adds a twinned entry? The hand-edit path across RuleCases and the probe was not exercised, by design.
what_went_wrong: The backlog item aged about 22 slices (SL-031 to SL-053) carrying '7 settled'. When it opened, the failure it predicted had already happened: C-001 and C-003 were red (28 vs 32, 29 vs 33), unseen because no gate runs the suite. SL-043 had hand-refreshed the pins once before.

build-check ran twice. The first pass halted on a 'partial' survey where every criterion was missing, which is the expected state before building. A person had to override with 'built anyway'. The slice had no acceptance list, so the build-check wrote its own criteria and then halted on them.

The design's central oracle (Fitness rule count shared with C-007) was overturned by a person's decision (O-015) and never built. Its must-verify preconditions (run C-007, run a lone -Case) each cost one command but were left as obligations O-010, O-012 and O-013 instead of being run in design.

The design said 'throwaway probe'. The engine's obligation model needs persistent test commands, so build shipped a permanent 96 s, 9-shape script. It pins 11/15/27 a second time and the exact source lines of rules-parity.ps1:632-633. The slice meant to remove pins added new ones, and nothing reruns the probe.

Critique and critique-review both recorded no account at low tier. The record cannot say what, if anything, they checked, and the design's 'nobody has disagreed with this' flag went unanswered until a person decided O-015.

The guard rule's 'because' text is engine-appended at design acceptance and cannot follow build deviations. It still names the Fitness rule count as the oracle after O-015 replaced it, so the drift stands (code-review, fitness.yaml:600-604).

The ID 'O-005' means two different things in this slice: the project-level 'no gate runs the suite' gap, and SL-053's own discharged case obligation. Stage reports call it open while the obligations list shows it discharged.
